description:
Design doc section 4 draws 'primary helium loop' and 'steam generator' as separate DAG nodes. In the code the SG is INSIDE the primary loop phase -- advance_steam_generator (primary_loop.rs:820) is called from it.

Consequence if uncorrected: the kernel boundary gets drawn between primary and
SG where the code has none, leaving a 0.0%-of-compute 'primary loop' kernel
while the real cost sits inside it.

Also correct section 4's inference that the outer correctors 'suggest ... some
subsystems may be evaluable concurrently'. They are a fixed-point iteration that
rewinds and re-advances the SAME chain, so they make the DAG more serial, not
less.

Evidence: op-276r.1, GH #148 comment.
title: Correct section 4 of docs/architecture/htgr-sim-execution.md: SG is inside the primary loop

description: Workspace-wide rule: any individual test whose runtime exceeds 5 minutes must be gated with #[cfg_attr(not(feature = "long-tests"), ignore)]. The long-tests feature is ON by default in every crate that declares it, so a plain cargo test runs the long suite; --no-default-features turns it off for fast iteration. Codify as a HARD RULE in the workspace CLAUDE.md.
title: Gate >5 min tests behind a default-on long-tests feature

description:
RegularMesh::shannon_entropy (tally/mesh.rs:200) was ported from OpenMC and verified to 3 ulp against its own bank on 2026-09-17, but has NO caller outside tests/shannon_entropy_vs_openmc.rs.

Wiring is not free: it takes &[BankSite] (particle/bank.rs:12) while all THREE k drivers bank into their own private struct Site - transport_csg.rs:89, keff.rs:199, keff_delta.rs:149 - and never expose the bank. Needs a conversion or a per-generation callback.

A loosely-coupled 1.8 m pebble core is exactly where source convergence bites, and the RMC paper's own 5 inactive cycles are not a model to copy.
title: Phase 3.1: wire Shannon entropy into the k-eigenvalue drivers

description:
ACTION ON THE MAINTAINER. The maintainer will supply digitised data points read off the decay-heat graphs in Tobias, A., "Decay heat", Progress in Nuclear Energy. These become the GOLDEN ORACLE for two separate pieces of work at once:

1. THE DECAY-HEAT MODEL (crates/teh-o-prke/src/decay_heat.rs). As of 2026-08-11 that module implements the 23-group 1978 draft ANS Standard fit from Tobias Table 16, and its unit tests verify the implementation against the paper OWN EQUATIONS (eq. 32 burst function, eq. 33 integral form) plus the total decay energy per fission. That is VERIFICATION - is it implemented correctly - and nothing more. There is currently NO comparison against an independent curve. Digitised plot points would turn this into a real check: reconstruct the published decay-heat curve from the 23-group parameters and compare against the digitised points from the same paper figures.

2. THE KOVAN GRAPH DIGITISER (see the sibling bead). The same digitised points are the acceptance test for the digitiser itself: run the digitiser over the Tobias figures and compare its output against the maintainer hand-digitised values. A digitiser with no ground truth is unfalsifiable.

WHY ONE DATASET SERVES BOTH: it is the same figures. Points read by hand validate the tool; the tool then scales to figures nobody wants to read by hand.

WHAT IS NEEDED, per figure supplied:
- which figure (number and page) in which document
- the axis calibration used (linear or log on each axis, and the two reference points per axis)
- the digitised (x, y) pairs
- an estimate of reading uncertainty - on a log axis this is NOT uniform and matters
- who digitised it and when

PROVENANCE (DATA_POLICY.md): digitisation is a PROCESSING STEP and must be documented as one. The scoping docs already flag that HTR-10 safety demonstration test data will arrive as digitised plots rather than tables, so getting this discipline right here pays off later.

The Tobias source PDF is at kovan_import/decay heat tobias.pdf and has NOT yet been catalogued into kovan - its access tier needs deciding first (Progress in Nuclear Energy is Elsevier, so most likely proprietary; the numerical parameters are facts and usable either way, only redistribution of the PDF is gated).
title: MAINTAINER TO SUPPLY: digitised Tobias decay-heat plots as the golden oracle

description:
Observed 2026-09-11 in outram-park-backend. Recording here per the CLAUDE.md rule that every kopitiam/kopi-beans rough edge gets written up and never silently worked around.

SYMPTOM. Every bn command failed with:
  invalid field value: state.jsonl: bead entries out of order at line 1499: prev=BeadId("op-zy3"), next=BeadId("op-cral")
and after that was fixed, the same class of error on notes.jsonl:
  note entries out of order at line 826: prev=NoteOrderKey{bead_id: op-zy3,...}, next=NoteOrderKey{bead_id: op-b2k,...}

CAUSE. Commit 0a4097e on refs/heads/beads/store, 'beads(store): reconcile diverged store (by-id union of local and remote, nothing dropped)' (authored by a Claude session 2026-09-10), appended the union's new records at end-of-file instead of inserting them in sorted position. 1 record in state.jsonl (op-cral) and 5 in notes.jsonl (op-b2k, op-cjw.1, op-cjw.14, op-cjw.9, op-cral). Data was intact; only the ordering invariant was broken.

REPRODUCED ON bn 0.1.7 AND 0.1.9 identically, so this is the store, not a reader regression.

THE UPSTREAM GAP — this is what to file. There is no first-party way to repair it:
  - 'bn store migrate --dry-run', the documented repair path, fails with the SAME reader error before it can do anything.
  - 'bn store fsck' is WAL-scoped, requires --store-id, and does not address checkpoint jsonl ordering.
So a store with a single mis-ordered line is bricked for every client, with no built-in recovery. Ask upstream for a reader-independent repair/normalise command (e.g. 'bn store repair --reorder'), and ideally for the writer to insert in sorted position (or sort on flush) so this cannot be produced in the first place.

SECOND, SMALLER ISSUE: 'cargo install kopi-beans --version 0.1.7' fails to resolve because a transitive dependency version is yanked; --locked is required. Worth mentioning upstream.

ALSO NOTE for whoever files it: the legacy refs/heads/beads/store is what the daemon hydrates from, while the canonical store is the sharded checkpoint at refs/beads/<store_id>/core. Repairing the legacy ref alone appears to do nothing until the local hydration cache under ~/.local/share/beads-rs/stores/<store_id>/ is cleared and the daemon restarted. That is non-obvious and cost real time; worth asking upstream to surface it.

ACTION: file as a GitHub issue on theodoreOnzGit/kopitiam (needs add_repo first — kopitiam is outside this repo's default session scope). Fallback if gh is unavailable: docs/kopitiam-issues/kopi-beans-store-out-of-order-unrepairable.md. Filing the issue ends our involvement — do not follow it with a patch; kopitiam/kopi-beans are consumed as released binaries only and must never be edited from this workspace.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content: Duplicate of op-9nhu, filed ~20 min earlier on the same defect. op-9nhu was itself one of the 10 beads recovered by the store repair, so it was invisible in the tracker when this bead was written. All evidence here has been added as a comment on op-9nhu; upstream reporting is tracked there.

title: kopi-beans: store unreadable and unrepairable after an out-of-order append; file upstream
